facts.statement: The genus Thoracosaurus was first described by Leidy in 1852.
facts.quote: authority: Leidy, 1852

facts.statement: Thoracosaurus fossils date from the Late Cretaceous to the Early Paleocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous - Early Paleocene,

facts.statement: This extinct genus, known as the chest lizard, lived in North America and Europe during the Late Cretaceous and Early Paleocene.
facts.quote: Thoracosaurus (chest lizard) is an extinct genus of long-snouted eusuchian which existed during the Late Cretaceous and Early Paleocene in North America and Europe.

facts.statement: Thoracosaurus was a long-snouted eusuchian crocodilian.
facts.quote: Thoracosaurus (chest lizard) is an extinct genus of long-snouted eusuchian

facts.statement: Research beginning in the 1990s placed Thoracosaurus within Gavialoidea, excluding modern false gharials.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic work starting in the 1990s instead supported affinities within Gavialoidea exclusive of such forms

facts.statement: A 2018 study suggests Thoracosaurus might have been a non-crocodylian eusuchian, though this is debated.
facts.quote: although a 2018 tip dating study simultaneously using morphological, molecular (DNA sequencing), and stratigraphic (fossil age) data suggests that it might have been a non-crocodylian eusuchian.

facts.statement: The genus includes the type species T. neocesariensis from North America and T. isorhynchus or T. macrorhynchus from Europe.
facts.quote: The genus contains the type species Thoracosaurus neocesariensis in North America, and what is either Thoracosaurus isorhynchus or Thoracosaurus macrorhynchus from Europe

facts.statement: A recent review argues that T. macrorhynchus is a junior synonym of T. isorhynchus.
facts.quote: a recent review argues that T. macrorhynchus is a junior synonym of T. isorhynchus

facts.statement: If European and North American forms cannot be differentiated, T. isorhynchus would be considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: if not, then T. isorhynchus would be a nomen dubium

facts.statement: Many species have been assigned to Thoracosaurus, but most are considered dubious.
facts.quote: A number of species have been referred to this genus, but most are dubious.

facts.statement: Thoracosaurus belongs to the superfamily Gavialoidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Gavialoidea

facts.statement: The genus authority for Thoracosaurus is Leidy, 1852.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Leidy, 1852

facts.statement: The genus includes the type species T. neocesariensis, as well as T. macrorhynchus and T. scanicus.
facts.quote: subdivision: T. neocesariensis (de Kay, 1842 [originalmente Gavialis neocesariensis]) (especie tipo) T. macrorhynchus T. scanicus

facts.statement: Thoracosaurus was an extinct gavialoid crocodilian that lived during the Late Cretaceous and the beginning of the Paleocene.
facts.quote: Thoracosaurus es un género extinto de crocodiliano gavialoideo el cual vivió durante el Cretácico Superior y el inicio del Paleoceno.

facts.statement: T. scanicus was a relatively large gavialoid with a body length of over 4.4 meters and a skull 55 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Thoracosaurus scanicus era un gavialoideo relativamente grande, con una longitud corporal de más de 4.4 metros y un cráneo de 55 centímetros.

facts.statement: The time range for Thoracosaurus is from the Santonian to the Ypresian, between 85.7 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Ypresian (85.7 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Thoracosaurus is the family Gavialidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gavialidae

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Thoracosaurus is T. neocesariensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Thoracosaurus neocesariensis

facts.statement: There are 53 recorded fossil occurrences of Thoracosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 53

facts.statement: Thoracosaurus is thought to have lived in marine environments.
facts.quote: It is thought to have inhabited marine environments.

facts.statement: A redescription and study on the affinities of T. isorhynchus was published by Boerman et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: Redescription and a study on the affinities of Thoracosaurus isorhynchus is published by Boerman et al. (2026).
